Hi Liam — thanks for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

1) Goals from your side
- Replace current multi-model routing layer with a single policy-driven gateway to manage latency/cost SLOs and fallback chains;
- Add structured outputs (tool-calling style) for invoice extraction and classification;
- Surface embedding-based semantic search + reranker for Q&A over product docs.

2) High-level architecture we discussed
- Client apps call Acme Gateway -> Redwood SDK (client) -> Redwood Inference (region-specific endpoints).
- SDK handles auth (API key + optional mTLS) and request metadata (region, priority).
- Model routing done by a policy service: route by latency SLO, cost tier, and content policy; fallback chains to cheaper quantized variants.

3) Immediate technical asks from your infra team
- SDK quickstart + example for server-side (Node) + browser flows.
- Sample config for policy rules: e.g., requests <150ms SLO -> low-latency model; long docs -> embedding+rerank.
- Clarify auth options (API keys vs mTLS vs OIDC).

- Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive with Acme infra + Redwood runtime engineers — propose Mon 26 Jul 10am PT.

Hi Liam / Nina — quick follow-up from the runtime side to address the OIDC/mTLS question and the latency/cost tradeoffs you called out. High-level notes below; we'll go deeper in the tech deep-dive.

1) SDK & auth\- The Redwood client SDK supports: API keys, OIDC via token exchange (we provide an exchange endpoint for your auth provider), and mTLS for server-to-server. For browser flows we recommend using OIDC + short-lived tokens to avoid embedding secrets. We'll include an example using Auth0 and a token-exchange snippet in the quickstart.

2) Routing & policy config (example)\- Policy file (YAML/JSON) can express rules by request metadata:
  - priority: "low|standard|realtime"
  - max_latency_ms: integer target
  - cost_tier: "standard|reduced"
  - model_family: preference list (gptx-large, gptx-medium-quantized, open-embed-256)

Example rule (informal):
  - if priority==realtime and request.tokens < 500 then route -> gptx-large (gpu-low-latency)
  - else if document_length > 2000 tokens then route -> embed+rerank (cpu/embedding-pool)
  - fallback chain: gptx-large -> gptx-medium-quantized -> gptx-small-quantized -> safety-filter

3) Latency vs batching/cache\- For 100-150ms P95 you need:
  - colocated regional endpoints (we'll route to us-west by default for your users),
  - small batch sizes and priority queues (realtime priority bypasses batching),
  - warm KV cache for repeated prefixes (we can pre-warm based on traffic patterns).

4) Embeddings + reranker pattern\- Typical flow: index docs with embeddings (128/256 dims), do approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search to get top-N candidates, then run reranker (small LM or cross-encoder) for final ranking. We can host the ANN index and reranker in the same region to keep latencies low.

Attachments: a short policy example and SDK snippet included (redwood-sdk-quickstart.md attached).

Proposed deliverables before the deep-dive:
- Redwood: full SDK quickstart (Node + browser), token-exchange example, sample policy YAML, and a short demo app (Dev / Marissa) — Thu EOD.
- Acme: sample payload + doc set (Liam / Nina) — Fri EOD.

I'll pick time slots for Mon and send invites for the deep-dive (include runtime, infra, and infra-security).

Thanks,
